findings.proposedIrEvidence: conditions[0] permits sale/transfer 'to the counterparty Person or to any other Person', but condition[1] then requires as a separate listed condition: 'Such other Person is one to whom funds have been or are to be advanced by the counterparty Person on the security of such property or of the rental obligations...' No OR operator connects condition[1] to the first branch.
findings.sourceEvidence: which has been or is to be sold or transferred by the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary to such Person or to any other Person to whom funds have been or are to be advanced by such Person on the security of such property or rental obligations of the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary
findings.verifierReasoning: In the source, the 'or' creates two disjunctive transfer scenarios: (i) sale/transfer to the original arrangement counterparty ('such Person'), or (ii) sale/transfer to some other Person who received funds advanced by that counterparty on the security of the property or rental obligations. The IR's flat, conjunctive condition list makes the second scenario ('such other Person... advanced funds') a precondition for every prohibited arrangement. A direct sale-and-leaseback to the original counterparty, with no second Person receiving advances, would therefore not be captured by the encoded rule even though it is plainly within the source prohibition unless the FMV exception applies. This changes the scope of the covenant and is material.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: condition[1] states the advance is 'on the security of such property or of the rental obligations', but condition[2] independently requires: 'The rental obligations given as security are those of the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary.'
findings.sourceEvidence: on the security of such property or rental obligations of the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary
findings.verifierReasoning: The source creates an alternative: the advance can be secured by 'such property' OR by 'rental obligations of the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary.' The IR's separate condition[2] requires the rental obligations of the borrower group to be the security. If an arrangement is secured only by the property itself, condition[2] would not be satisfied and the arrangement would not be treated as prohibited, even though the source reaches it via the 'such property' branch. This is an OR-to-AND distortion and is material.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The conditions in ir-rule:253390261ce52155990b32d2 are: property has been/is to be sold or transferred; an 'other Person' has received or will receive funds advanced by the counterparty on the security of the property or rental obligations; and the rental obligations given as security are those of the Parent Borrower or a Subsidiary. No condition or structured element states that the arrangement must provide for the leasing by the Parent Borrower or a Subsidiary.
findings.sourceEvidence: Enter into any arrangement with any Person providing for the leasing by the Parent Borrower or any Subsidiary of real or personal property
findings.verifierReasoning: The core scope of the covenant is a sale-and-leaseback: an arrangement that provides for leasing by the borrower group. The IR's condition list does not include that element. As a result, the encoded prohibition could capture arrangements that involve a sale and financing but no lease to the Parent Borrower or Subsidiary, or, combined with the other condition issues, may mis-describe which leaseback arrangements are restricted. A competent reviewer would need this element to determine whether a transaction is prohibited; its absence is a material omission.
